title: How a Sink P-Trap Blocks Sewer Gas
description: A sink P-trap is a critical component of fixture drainage designed to maintain a permanent water seal. As wastewater flows down the sink drain, gravity pushes the bulk of the water into the branch line, but a specific volume remains trapped in the curved dip of the pipe. This standing water creates an airtight liquid barrier between the open drain outlet and the main drainage network. By preventing hazardous sewer gases like methane and hydrogen sulfide from rising back into the building, the P-trap safeguards indoor air quality while allowing solid waste and liquid to flow through smoothly under normal gravity.

By preventing hazardous sewer gases like methane and hydrogen sulfide from rising back into the building, the P-trap safeguards indoor air quality while allowing solid waste and liquid to flow through smoothly under normal gravity.
